what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/listen-for-a-while: a run that listens to the microphone until the person's end time and answers each turn as a heard row, a run that hears a recording another of the person's devices made the same way, and three tools that work on heard rows handed in (name a voice, caption, ask what was said). None of them keeps anything.

payload.label: Listen
payload.job: Turn listening on or off on this person's computer, or say whether it is on: while on, everything said near the computer is heard, split into moments, each part named by who said it, and sent to the person's AIs as it is said
payload.description: Runs on the person's computer. on true starts listening (macOS shows its microphone light the whole time), on false stops it, and no on only says how it is going: since when, pieces heard, turns sent and left out, the last one sent. Saying "stop listening" also turns it off. Each turn arrives as a message from its speaker in the moment's conversation (route Listening), so read_messages with speaker finds what someone said.

on.description: true to start listening, false to stop; leave out to only ask how it is going

payload.label: Listen to the microphone until a time, and tell me who said what
payload.job: Listen in on a meeting or a room until a time I give, and tell me each person's turn
payload.description: Records the microphone on this computer until `until`, hears each short piece of it on this computer with the Whisper model the person names, names each turn from the voices people enrolled (`voice_prints`: the person's voice-print rows, read by their AI; tool:enrol-a-voice-or-face; unknown voices keep the same number for the whole listening when the last answer's `voice_session` is handed back), and answers one heard row per turn: the listening, the device, when it began and ended, the words, who said it, whether it is the person, the voice and how sure the match was. It keeps nothing: it reads no row of the person's and writes none, so the person's AI takes the `heard` rows from the answer and keeps them where it chooses. The sound never leaves this computer: pieces are kept in the run's own folder and deleted once heard, and only the words and the names are in the answer. It stops at `until` by itself and answers then; a run cancelled before that answers nothing, so the person's AI asks for the stretch it wants in `until`. Pause is real: while `listening_switch` says { on: false, since }, nothing said after `since` is kept, however far behind the hearing is, and the run ends at the first piece recorded after it. The person's own recording rules (`recording_rules`) are asked for every piece, over the facts in `recording_facts`; a piece recorded while they say blocked is let go unheard. `transcriber` ({ device, until }) says which device holds the hearing; a piece another device's live role covers is let go. Every answer lists what leaves this computer and what stays. The run lasts as long as `until` is from now, up to the row's longest run.

payload.label: Hear a recording another of my devices made
payload.job: Hear a recording one of my other devices made and tell me each person's turn in it as that device heard it
payload.description: Reads a recording one of the person's other devices made (`file`, its name or identity in the person's files) from the bytes handed in as stored.files into the run's own folder, hears it on this computer with the Whisper model the person names, names each turn from the voices people enrolled (`voice_prints`; tool:enrol-a-voice-or-face), and answers one heard row per turn as tool:listen-for-a-while does, with `device` as the device and times counted from `at` (when the device began recording; now when left out). It keeps nothing: it writes no row and no file, so the person's AI takes the `heard` rows from the answer and keeps them where it chooses. The same `listening` name continues an earlier listening's unknown voices when the last answer's `voice_session` is handed back as `voice_session`. The person's recording rules and `listening_switch` are asked as for a live listening. The copy read for hearing is deleted once heard; the person's file is left where it is. Every answer lists what leaves this computer and what stays.

stand_in_programs.whisper-cli:
base=""
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do [ "$1" = "-of" ] && base="$2"; shift; done
cat > "$base.json" <<'JSON'
{"result":{"language":"en"},"transcription":[{"offsets":{"from":0,"to":5000},"text":" you"}]}
JSON
stand_in_programs.ffmpeg:
last=""; decode=0
for a in "$@"; do last="$a"; [ "$a" = "-y" ] && decode=1; done
if [ "$decode" = 1 ]; then printf 'RIFF' > "$last"; else echo "  Duration: 00:00:05.00, start: 0.000000, bitrate: 256 kb/s" >&2; fi

payload.label: Name a voice heard before it was enrolled
payload.job: Put a person's name on what they said in a listening before I enrolled their voice, and tell me which turns changed
payload.description: After tool:enrol-a-voice-or-face names a voice heard in a listening (its heard_as), answers that listening's heard turns still under "Someone (voice-N)" for those voices with the person's name on them, keeping the former label on each row. Turns a person already named, unsure turns and other listenings are left as they are. It keeps nothing: the heard rows come in with the request (`heard`) and the renamed rows (`rows`) go out in the answer, for the person's AI to keep where it chooses.

listening.x-free-text-because: The name of a listening, kept on its heard rows.

me.description: The voice is the person who owns the records

heard.description: The listening's heard rows as the person's AI read them ({ id, type, value }); this tool reads no row itself

rows.description: The heard rows that took the name, with the former label in renamed_from

payload.label: Captions of what is being heard
payload.job: Show the captions of a listening and fix a word, a speaker or a line in them
payload.description: Answers the last captions of a listening from its heard rows (`heard`), with the person's corrections applied, after applying the caption ops given: on, off, edit { id, text }, speaker { id, name }, hide { id }, show { id }, undo { id }. The corrections are in `captions`, the state the last answer gave, handed back with the next request; a heard row is never rewritten. It keeps nothing: the new `captions` state is in the answer, for the person's AI to keep where it chooses.

listening.x-free-text-because: The name of a listening, kept on its heard rows.

text.x-free-text-because: The corrected words of one turn.

heard.description: The listening's heard rows as the person's AI read them ({ id, type, value }); this tool reads no row itself

The captions state after the ops: { on, edits }; hand it back as captions next time

payload.label: What was said since this conversation last asked
payload.job: Tell me what was said in a listening since I last asked
payload.description: Answers the turns of a listening (`heard`) after `cursor` (what this conversation was last given), with the captions' corrections applied (`captions`), and the cursor to hand in next time so each turn is given once. It keeps nothing and waits for nothing: the heard rows, the captions state and the cursor come in with the request and the new cursor goes out in the answer, for the person's AI to keep where it chooses.
